name: F-14D Tomcat
role: Two-seat carrier-based long-range fleet air defence fighter

serviceWindow.statusNotes: The US Navy retired the F-14 in 2006 (retirement ceremony 22 September 2006, last flight 4 October 2006). No US Navy F-14D exists on the 2026-03-15 scenario date, so any scenario that fields one is a what-if. The record shows the aircraft as it flew in its last years of service.

propulsionSummary: Two General Electric F110-GE-400 afterburning turbofans, each rated at 26,950 lbf (about 120 kN) with afterburner.

weapons.name: AIM-54C Phoenix
weapons.mountSummary: Carried on the fuselage tunnel stations and under the glove pylons. The F-14 can carry up to 6 Phoenix; the engine loadout counts 4.

weapons.name: AIM-120C AMRAAM
weapons.mountSummary: Underwing or glove stations. AMRAAM integration on the F-14D was limited, so treat the pairing with Phoenix as our scenario assumption.

sensors.name: AN/APG-71 radar
sensors.role: Long-range air search and multi-target track, able to guide several Phoenix missiles at once

sensors.name: AAX-1 Television Camera Set (TCS)
sensors.role: Long-range optical identification of aircraft without using the radar

sensors.name: AN/ALR-67 radar warning receiver
sensors.role: Passive detection of hostile radar emissions

sensors.name: Crew visual lookout
sensors.role: Visual identification of aircraft and ships in clear weather

loadouts.name: Fleet air defence, long-range Phoenix fit
loadouts.role: Carrier group air defence against bombers and cruise missile launch platforms

loadouts.name: Typical Cold War fleet air defence fit
loadouts.role: Barrier combat air patrol with mixed long-, medium- and short-range missiles

radar.note: A large twin-engine swing-wing fighter with no radar-reducing shaping, so it gives a strong return from most angles.

infrared.note: Two big afterburning turbofans make a strong heat source, especially from behind.

visual.note: A large airframe about 19 m long with a wide wing span when unswept, easy to see against the sky.

brief.whatItIs: The F-14D Tomcat was the last and best version of the US Navy's big swing-wing fleet defence fighter. It had a pilot and a radar officer, stronger F110 engines than earlier models, and a newer radar. It was built to protect a carrier group by shooting down enemy bombers from far away. The Navy retired the whole F-14 fleet in 2006, so in this scenario it is a what-if aircraft.
brief.howItIsUsed: A commander used the Tomcat as the outer layer of carrier defence. Pairs flew combat air patrols out along the likely approach path of enemy aircraft, with the radar officer tracking many targets at once and the pilot firing the long-range AIM-54 Phoenix missile when targets were still beyond 100 nautical miles. The wings sweep back for speed and forward for slow carrier landings and long loiter time. Its strengths are radar reach, missile range and the number of targets it can engage together. Its weaknesses are a large radar and infrared signature, high fuel burn and heavy maintenance demands. Enemy fighters with their own long-range missiles, or a lack of tanker support, can cut its effective reach sharply.
typicalMissions: Fleet air defence and barrier combat air patrol
Long-range interception of bombers and maritime patrol aircraft
Precision strike with laser-guided bombs in its late years
